Q3235459.label: 1991 Mexican legislative election
Q3235459.desc: composition of Mexican Chamber of Deputies
Q3235459.summary: Legislative elections were held in Mexico on 18 August 1991, alongside gubernatorial elections in six states. The Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) won 320 of the 500 seats in the Chamber of Deputies and 31 of the 32 seats up for election in the Senate. Voter turnout was 61% in the Chamber election and 62% in the Senate election.

Q5174915.label: 1944 Costa Rican general election
Q5174915.desc: General election held in Costa Rica
Q5174915.summary: General elections were held in Costa Rica on 13 February 1944 to elect the president and half of the Constitutional Congress. Teodoro Picado Michalski of the Victory Bloc won the presidential election with 66% of the vote. Voter turnout was 84%.

mentions.c: Costa Rica: 1944 Costa Rican general election

Q6544003.label: February 1953 Liechtenstein general election
Q6544003.summary: General elections were held in Liechtenstein on 15 February 1953 to elect the 15 members of the Landtag. The Progressive Citizens' Party (FBP) won eight seats and retained its majority, while the Patriotic Union (VU) won seven. Voter turnout was 90.5%.

Q45808771.label: Hartwig Löger
Q45808771.desc: Austrian politician, businessman, former secretary for finance and vice federal chancellor
Q45808771.summary: Hartwig Löger is an Austrian politician and former business executive who served as minister of finance from 2017 to 2019. From 2011 to 2017 he was chief executive officer of UNIQA Austria.

Q12025475.label: Jiří Rusnok
Q12025475.summary: Jiří Rusnok is a Czech politician and economist who served as the prime minister of the Czech Republic between June 2013 and January 2014. From 2016 to 2022 he served as the governor of the Czech National Bank.

Q2069123.label: 1955 Maltese general election
Q2069123.summary: General elections were held in Malta between 26 and 28 February 1955. The Malta Labour Party remained the largest party, winning 23 of the 40 seats.

Q1259139.label: Croatian European Union membership referendum
Q1259139.summary: A referendum on the EU accession of the Republic of Croatia was held on 22 January 2012. Croatia finished accession (membership) negotiations on 30 June 2011 and signed the Treaty of Accession on 9 December 2011, setting it on course to become the bloc's 28th member state.

Q106555011.label: 2026 Kosovan presidential election
Q106555011.summary: The Assembly of Kosovo held an indirect election for president on 6 October 2026.

Q752259.label: Bulgarian Socialist Party
Q752259.summary: The Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP), also known as The Centenarian, is a centre-left, social democratic political party in Bulgaria. The BSP is a member of the Socialist International, Party of European Socialists, and Progressive Alliance. Although founded in 1990 in its modern form, it traces its political heritage back to the founding of the BRSDP in 1891. It is also Bulgaria's largest party by membership numbers.

Member of: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats

Q39088259.label: 2019 Romanian presidential election
Q39088259.summary: Presidential elections were held in Romania on 10 November 2019, with a second round held on 24 November 2019. They were the eighth presidential election held in post-1989 Romania. Incumbent president Klaus Iohannis, first elected in the 2014 election, was eligible for re-election.

Q738947.label: Estonian Reform Party
Q738947.summary: The Estonian Reform Party is a liberal political party in Estonia. The party has been led by Kristen Michal since 2024. It is colloquially known as the "Squirrel Party" or as "the Squirrels", referencing its logo.

Member of: Alliance of Liberals and Democrats for Europe Party

Q2060419.label: Battle of Brunete
Q2060419.desc: 1937 battle of the Spanish Civil War
Q2060419.summary: The Battle of Brunete, fought 24 kilometres (15 mi) west of Madrid, was a Republican attempt to alleviate the pressure exerted by the Nationalists on the capital and on the north during the Spanish Civil War. Although initially successful, the Republicans were forced to retreat from Brunete after Nationalist counterattacks, and suffered devastating casualties from the battle.

Q177283.label: Altmark Incident
Q177283.desc: 1940 WW II naval incident between British and German ships
Q177283.summary: The Altmark incident was a naval incident of World War II between British destroyers and the German tanker Altmark, which happened on 16–17 February 1940. It took place in what were neutral Norwegian waters. On board the Altmark were roughly 300 Allied prisoners, whose ships had been sunk by the pocket battleship Graf Spee in the Southern Atlantic Ocean.

Q700547.label: Operation Vengeance
Q700547.desc: 1943 American military operation to kill Japanese Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto
Q700547.summary: Operation Vengeance was the American military operation to kill Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto of the Imperial Japanese Navy on 18 April 1943 during the Solomon Islands campaign in the Pacific Theater of World War II. Yamamoto, commander of the Combined Fleet of the Imperial Japanese Navy, was killed near Bougainville Island when his G4M1 transport aircraft was shot down by United States Army Air Forces fighter aircraft operating from Kukum Field on Guadalcanal.

Q486531.label: Battle of Unsan
Q486531.summary: The Battle of Unsan, also known as the Battle of Yunshan, was a series of engagements of the Korean War that took place from 25 October to 4 November 1950 near Unsan, North Pyongan province in present-day North Korea. As part of the People's Republic of China's First Phase Campaign, the People's Volunteer Army (PVA) repeatedly attacked the Republic of Korea Army (ROKA) 1st Infantry Division near Unsan beginning on 25 October, to surprise the advancing United Nations Command (UNC).

Q4871299.label: Battle of Jaffna
Q4871299.summary: The Battle of Jaffna was fought from October to December 1995 for the city of Jaffna.

mentions.c: Part of Sri Lankan Civil War

Q2105475.label: Battle of Azaz
Q2105475.img: Azaz Syria during the Syrian Civil War Displacement with Tractor.jpg
Q2105475.summary: The Battle of Azaz took place between the Syrian Arab Army and the Free Syrian Army for control of the city of Azaz, north of Aleppo, during the early insurgency phase of the Syrian civil war.

Q117866115.label: Operation Raus aus Khartum
Q117866115.summary: Operation Raus aus Khartum was an evacuation operation of German and other armed forces during the 2023 Sudan conflict. The operation lasted from April 23 to April 25, 2023. A total of 8 flights evacuated 740 people, including 200 Germans. The Bundeswehr flew out people from around 30 nations, including 90 Canadians and 40 Dutchmen as well as around 30 Jordanians. The operation went without incident. The Sudanese authorities had been informed in advance through diplomatic channels.

Q21257859.label: Andrew Garbarino
Q21257859.summary: Andrew Reed Garbarino is an American attorney and politician serving as the U.S. representative for New York's 2nd congressional district since 2021. A member of the Republican Party, he served as the New York State Assemblyman for the 7th district from 2013 to 2020.

Positions held: member of the New York State Assembly

Q1069187.label: Kishū Domain
Q1069187.desc: Japanese historical estate in Kii province
Q1069187.summary: The Kishū Domain, also referred to as Kii Domain or Wakayama Domain, was a feudal domain in Kii Province, Japan. This domain encompassed regions in present-day Wakayama and southern Mie prefectures and had a substantial income of 555,000 koku. The administrative center of the domain was located at Wakayama Castle, which is situated in present-day Wakayama, Wakayama Prefecture.

Q1965699.label: Cambridge Observatory
Q1965699.desc: astronomical observatory at the University of Cambridge in the East of England
Q1965699.summary: Cambridge Observatory is an astronomical observatory of the University of Cambridge on Madingley Road in western Cambridge, England. Established in 1823, it forms part of the site of the Institute of Astronomy. Its original building is Grade II listed and houses the Institute's astronomical library.

mentions.c: An eclipse confirms that gravity bends light (1919)

Q82563.label: Leon Cooper
Q82563.summary: Leon N. Cooper was an American theoretical physicist and neuroscientist who shared the 1972 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on superconductivity. Cooper developed the concept of Cooper pairs and collaborated with John Bardeen and John Robert Schrieffer to develop the BCS theory of conventional superconductivity. In neuroscience, Cooper co-developed the BCM theory of synaptic plasticity.

Q9091203.label: ultraconservatism
Q9091203.summary: Ultraconservatism refers to extreme conservative views in politics or religious practice. In modern politics, ultraconservative usually refers to conservatives of the far-right on the political spectrum, comprising groups or individuals who are located to the right of those who hold mainstream conservative views, and continuing further right to include fringe parties.

Q1628291.label: Social Democracy of the Republic of Poland
aliases: Social Democracy of the Republic of Poland (SdRP)
Q1628291.wiki: Social Democracy of the Republic of Poland
Q1628291.summary: Social Democracy of the Republic of Poland was a social democratic political party in Poland created in 1990, shortly after the Revolutions of 1989. The party was the main party of the successor parties to the Polish United Workers' Party (PZPR).

Q269443.label: Kemalism
Q269443.desc: founding ideology of the Republic of Turkey, proclaimed in 1923
Q269443.summary: Kemalism or Atatürkism is a political ideology based on the ideas of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the founder and first president of Turkey. Its symbol is the Six Arrows.
